concurrency.rule: If available Codex concurrency is lower than 32, every assignment is still created and queued. When a task finishes, the next queued task starts immediately.
startOrder: SRC01-SRC04 and every PF lane holding families start together — the conveyor and the builders are not sequential
VF lanes start on the first PF checkpoint, not on a completed assignment
FIX lanes start on the first FAIL_REPAIR_REQUIRED verdict
an empty PF lane starts the moment a source lane releases a family into it
concurrency.idleRule: A lane is idle only when no executable work exists for its kind. An empty PF lane at dispatch is idle because the source queue is empty for it, and the source lanes are the work that ends that.

rasterRule: **A missing Chromium is not a source blocker and it is not a legal blocker.** ENV-RAS01 established that this container cannot resolve or fetch one -- the Playwright CDN answers HTTP 403 from inside Codex. That is an environment fact about the container, not a fact about the packet, and classifying it as BLOCKED_SOURCE would put a packet defect on a record that has none.
Finish every nonvisual obligation. Record the exact SHA-256 of the canonical and boundary PDFs you produced. Return the family `BUILT_RASTER_PENDING`.

`BUILT_RASTER_PENDING` is a factory workflow state and not a launch verdict. It zeroes nothing and waives nothing: visualDefects stays whatever it is, because it records that nobody has looked, not that there is nothing to see. **No packet becomes PASS_COMPLETE without RASTER_PASS.**

The render happens in `.github/workflows/rcap-packet-raster-acceptance-batch.yml` on a browser-equipped runner, against the exact bytes your hashes pin. RASTER_PASS sends the family to independent verification; RASTER_FAIL sends it to FIX.
Page rasters go through `scripts/raster/pdf-page-raster.mjs`. It discovers its own browser and calibrates the page-to-pixel mapping against both the paper bounds and stamped marks.
NEVER `pdftoppm`. NEVER `apt-get`. NEVER `playwright install`. The environment refuses package installation and a Poppler fallback is not a fallback, it is a different measurement.
The preflight now gates on the rasterizer resolving a browser it can execute, so a lane that cannot raster learns before it builds rather than after.
claimRule: Assert every family before reading or writing anything: `node scripts/grade-a-packet-factory-24h/claim.mjs --assert PF01 <familyId>`

The render happens in `.github/workflows/rcap-packet-raster-acceptance-batch.yml` on a browser-equipped runner, against the exact bytes your hashes pin. RASTER_PASS sends the family to independent verification; RASTER_FAIL sends it to FIX.

THE PACKET TELLS THE PARTICIPANT IT WROTE THEIR MAILING ADDRESS ONTO THE PETITION, AND IT DID NOT. Two participant-facing sentences say it did. The component table: 'the Massachusetts Probation Service Petition to Expunge itself, Rev. 10/11/2018, with your name, date of birth, MAILING ADDRESS and phone written in and every other blank left for you'. And the closing section: 'This is the official Massachusetts Probation Service Petition to Expunge with the FOUR facts the platform holds written into it'. There are three. reports/actual-writes.json reports 3 values in each fixture -- petitioner_name, date_of_birth, phone_number -- and I confirmed the absence on the delivered bytes rather than on the report: extracting page 1 of both fixtures with pdftotext -bbox-layout and reading the band that contains the mailing_address write box (field-map rect x=105 y=484 w=171 h=13, which is y_top 295-308 on a 792pt page), the only words present are the form's own printed captions 'Mailing Address:', 'City:', 'State:', 'Zip:' at x=28.42-100.93, 280.42, 415.42 and 514.42. The 171-point run from x=105 to x=276 is empty in the canonical fixture and empty in the boundary fixture. This is the A4 defect with its sign reversed -- the rule is that a packet may never tell a participant it does not state something it does state, and the harm here is the mirror image and worse in direction: a participant who reads the component table and believes the address is on the form will not transcribe it, and will file a petition with the Probation Service that has no address on it to answer. The packet contradicts itself three times over in the participant's favour -- 'Your address is not filled in, and that is deliberate', the street-address row in the items-to-supply table, and 'The whole address - street, city, state and zip' in the deliberately-left-blank list -- which is exactly why a reader cannot tell which sentence to believe. The fix is two words in two sentences, not a rebuild.

A repository-wide search finds that key only inside this family's own two artifacts and inside verifier return files that copied it; it is in no route record. The committed census names obligation:track-only:VA:va_seal_petition_misdemeanor for packetSetId va_seal_petition_misdemeanor-set, and product-wiring.json routeKey and routeKeys both carry that one. There is a real census route with a :petition-based-sealing suffix in Virginia - obligation:track-pathway:VA:va_seal_ancillary_matter_only:petition-based-sealing - which is a different track, so the printed key is not merely unregistered, it is confusable with another route's.

The packet says: 'Two things this packet does not tell you, because neither is established by the petition... The filing fee, and whether it can be waived. Ask the clerk of the circuit court above.' The committed route-obligation census states the fee posture for this exact route: its destination detail reads 'File the petition with no court fees or costs, serve the attorney for the Commonwealth of that locality, and separately request that the CCRE electronically forward...'. Not established by the petition is not the same as not established, and the record this family is bound to answers it. A participant is told to go and ask a clerk about a fee the record says does not exist.
